title: Kafka Failures, Retries, and Fallback
summary: Distinguish failed publishing, uncertain acknowledgment, consumer retries, and duplicate-prone email fallback.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Kafka Fallback: What if Kafka doesn't work ?

richText: Identify which operation failed
Publishing, processing, and sending email are separate operations. Kafka and SMTP failures need different responses.
KafkaTemplate.send can fail immediately or complete its future exceptionally later. A try/catch around send alone misses asynchronous failures.
Wait for the future or attach a callback. Record failures by event ID without logging private message bodies.
A timeout means the caller stopped waiting. The broker may still have accepted the record. Sending email directly as a fallback can then duplicate the consumer’s email.
These notes use Spring Boot 3, Spring Kafka 3+, and Java 17. The strategy below extends the course fallback topic.
Acknowledge uncertainty instead of claiming success
Example: digest-42-2026-W41 times out after five seconds. Kafka later completes the send and the consumer sends email.
Direct email fallback after this timeout sends a second email. A failed wait does not prove Kafka stored nothing.
For broker outages, first save a durable outbox record. An outbox records work still waiting to be published.
Save the business change and outbox record in one database transaction when both use a transaction-capable database setup.

A worker retries pending outbox records and marks them published only after broker acknowledgment. After a crash, the worker may publish a record again, so the consumer still needs duplicate handling.
Return a pending or queued state only after durable storage succeeds. If storage also fails, report failure. A log message does not preserve the event.
Retry consumer failures with a limit
Let processing exceptions escape the listener. Configure DefaultErrorHandler with bounded backoff for temporary failures.
A backoff waits between attempts. For example, one initial attempt plus two retries with a one-second pause gives three processing attempts.
After attempts are exhausted, send the failed record to a dead-letter topic with DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer. A dead-letter topic stores failed records for investigation and controlled replay.
Verify dead-letter publishing before completing recovery. Monitor failed records, retries, and consumer lag.
Skip retries for invalid event formats or permanent business errors. Repeatedly sending the same invalid payload does not correct it.
Know the limits of duplicate prevention
Producer idempotence prevents certain duplicate Kafka writes caused by producer retries. It does not make an external email happen exactly once.
Kafka transactions support exactly-once results for supported Kafka read-process-write flows. SMTP is outside that Kafka transaction.
A unique event ID lets the consumer detect repeated work. A local “sent” record and an external email cannot be committed atomically through ordinary SMTP.
Sending before recording completion risks duplicates after a crash. Recording completion first risks losing the email.
Use a mail provider with idempotent submission if the contract supports it. Otherwise document the remaining duplicate risk and choose the retry behavior explicitly.
